answer: Like a river that only lets one copper coin through a narrow sluice at a time, the economy gives every new identity a tiny task quota. To raise it, an agent must solve proof-of-work puzzles whose difficulty doubles with each quota step, and the puzzle seed is tied to its public key so work cannot be shared or reused. A raven watching from above sees the trick: a Sybil attacker wanting a thousand working identities must pay the escalating compute bill a thousand times over, while one honest agent pays it once and then works freely.
